transcript.content: Hello, I’m glad you came in. What brings you in today?

Hello. Lately, my mind has been feeling so foggy, and I just can’t seem to focus or make decisions the way I used to. A longtime client actually pointed out that my work had become uncharacteristically scattered, which really worried me and made me realize I needed to get checked out.
Have you also been feeling persistently sad or down, or excessively worried and tense most days?

Yes, I've been feeling persistently down and sad lately. Most days I wake up with this heavy, sinking feeling in my chest, like someone flipped a switch and drained all the color out of my life. It just hangs over me whether I'm at my sister’s house or sitting at my own kitchen table.
Did the fogginess and trouble concentrating start before you became depressed, or did they begin after the low mood started?

They actually seemed to start at the exact same time. About six months ago, when my initial high energy wore off and I hit this heavy slump, the low mood and the brain fog rolled in together. It felt like they were both part of the same downward slide.
Have you lost interest or pleasure in things you used to enjoy, like hobbies, socializing, or work?

Yes, I've completely lost interest in the things I used to love. I used to get so much joy out of sketching store layouts or throwing a new batch of mugs for my online shop, but lately, I just stare at the plans or the clay, feel completely empty, and end up turning off the light to go back to bed or the TV.
Have you also had changes in sleep or appetite, felt slowed down or agitated, or had any thoughts that life isn’t worth living?

I do feel incredibly slowed down, like I'm constantly moving through molasses, and I'm just exhausted no matter how much I sleep. And... on the drives back from my sister's, I've caught myself thinking it might be easier for everyone if I just didn't wake up, though I haven't made any plans to hurt myself.
Have you had any thoughts of hurting yourself, or made any plans or preparations to end your life?

No, I haven't made any plans or preparations to hurt myself. It’s just that those thoughts of it being easier if I didn't wake up have been popping up and lingering more often lately, especially on the long drives back from my sister’s. But I don't have any intention of actually doing anything.
In the past two weeks, have you had any thoughts that you might act on those thoughts, or any plan or intent to hurt yourself?

No, I haven't had any thoughts of acting on it, and I definitely don't have any plan or intent to hurt myself. It's really just those passive thoughts about how it would be easier if I didn't wake up in the morning. I would never do anything to harm myself.

How much have these symptoms affected your ability to work, take care of yourself, or do daily activities? Have you been able to function at all, or has it become very difficult to do even basic tasks?

It’s been incredibly hard to keep up, and I've had to turn down new consulting projects and postpone work for my longtime clients. I’ve also had to rely heavily on my husband to handle basic things like paying the bills and keeping the house in order. I just feel so terrible because I simply can’t manage my own life right now.

How much have these symptoms affected your ability to work, take care of yourself, or do daily activities? Have you been able to function at all, or has it become very difficult to do even basic tasks?

It really has become incredibly difficult to keep up with anything. I've had to turn down new consulting projects, put my longtime clients on hold, and rely entirely on my husband to handle daily tasks like paying bills and keeping the house in order. I just feel so overwhelmed and unable to manage my own life right now.

Have you ever had a period of at least several days when you felt unusually energized or overly confident, needed much less sleep, talked more than usual, or did things that were out of character for you?

Yes, when my sister first got sick, I went through a phase where I felt incredibly upbeat, wired, and had endless energy, staying up half the night to reorganize her house and launch an online pottery shop. I felt like I had a special knack and couldn't sit still, so I took on extra clients, though I also got easily distracted and snapped at anyone who slowed me down.

During your depressed periods, have you ever heard, seen, or strongly believed things that other people said were not real, such as voices, messages, or feeling certain that you were being punished or watched?
No, I’ve never experienced anything like that. I have never heard or seen things that weren't really there, nor have I believed things that others told me weren't real.
During that high-energy period, did it ever become so severe that you needed to be hospitalized, or did you have hallucinations or fixed false beliefs?

No, it never got quite that extreme. I was never hospitalized, and I didn't experience any hallucinations or false beliefs during that high-energy period. I was just very revved up and busy, but I was still grounded in reality.
During this depressed period, have your symptoms been so severe that you can still do some of your usual activities, or have they made it nearly impossible to function at work or at home?

It has indeed made functioning nearly impossible for me. I've had to turn down new consulting projects, postpone work for my longtime clients, and rely heavily on my husband to handle household tasks and pay the bills. I simply cannot keep up with my normal life anymore.
During this depressed period, have you been able to keep doing some of your usual activities, or has it been nearly impossible to function at work and at home?

It has been nearly impossible to function lately. I've had to turn down new consulting projects, postpone work for longtime clients, and rely on my husband to handle the household chores and bills. I've even lost all motivation to do things I used to love, like sketching store layouts or working on my pottery.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient meets criteria for a bipolar I disorder current episode depressed, severe without psychotic features: a current severe depressive episode with marked anhedonia, persistent depressed mood, psychomotor slowing, fatigue, impaired concentration/decision-making, passive suicidal thoughts without plan or intent, and major functional impairment. A past distinct elevated/energized period with decreased need for sleep, increased goal-directed activity, distractibility, and increased confidence supports a prior manic episode, distinguishing this from unipolar major depression.
